text:
observability-bot: ALERT: SLO burn - hosted-infer /v1/generate p99 latency 5.2s (15m window). SLO: p99 < 3s. Alerting because customer-facing errors rising. dashboard: https://redwood.internal/d/infra/hosted-infer-slo?orgId=1

marta-sre: seeing a related support escalation — ticket #54321 from AcmeCorp, reports timeouts followed by 502/500. They say it started ~09:12 UTC.

raj-support: copying ticket notes: \"client-side saw 500s ~09:12-09:27, then retries started getting 504, eventually succeeded on retry. Payloads are typical (chat completion). Attached sample request id: r:abcd-1234\"

emma-oncall: I pulled traces for r:abcd-1234 — trace exists but spans after gateway are missing (trace gap). Last span time = gateway.egress, no downstream service spans. Suspect connection reset between gateway and runtime or dropped kv cache path.

liang-platform: running log search now: `logs("service:gateway status>=500 route:\"/v1/generate\" | json | sort @timestamp desc | limit 50")`
- initial pattern: a cluster of `upstream reset` + `connection refused` around 09:14-09:20 UTC.

marta-sre: are these correlated with any deploys? deploy-bot: @deploy-bot any recent rollout?

deploy-bot: Deploy event: `runtime-service v2.14.1` rolled to canary at 09:10 UTC, 5% traffic. No full rollout. Logs show a handful of `handshake timeout` on canary pods.

raj-support: customer repro steps they provided: small prompt ~80 tokens, sync request, no streaming, single attempt. They said first attempt returns 500, immediate retry returns 200.

emma-oncall: reproduction on staging: I sent 50 requests at ~qps=2 with same payload. Saw ~3% 500s with identical gateway trace gap pattern. Attached minimal curl: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" -d '{"input":"hello"}'`

liang-platform: hypothesis: canary runtime pods with new kernel/network setting are intermittently dropping connections during TLS handshake under low concurrency. Kernel TLS offload + keepalive mismatch observed before. Query: `rate(requests{job=runtime,version=2.14.1,code=500}[5m])` spikes align with SLO window.

marta-sre: immediate ask: (1) throttle canary to 0% or rollback; (2) increase trace sampling to capture gateway->runtime handshakes for 10m; (3) create short-run repro in dedicated test pool.

liang-platform: rolling canary back to 0% now. Patch created: revert netstack tweak. Trace sampling bumped to 100% for runtime-service for 10m.

emma-oncall: opened internal incident ticket INC-2026-87, linked to customer ticket #54321. Adding timeline & initial findings.

raj-support: informed customer: said we're investigating and temporarily routing away from canary, ETA 30m. Customer asked for root cause follow-up.

marta-sre: followups: verify no authz/billing spikes (customer reported no billing issues), run grep on auth failures: `logs("status=401 OR status=403 | service:gateway")` — nothing abnormal. Also double-check rate-limiter logs for token throttle.

liang-platform: confirmed rate-limiter healthy, no token throttles for AcmeCorp. Also verified K8s pod restarts ≈ 0 for runtime canary pods during window.

emma-oncall: next steps for postmortem: gather network captures (tcpdump) from canary pod, kernel config diff between 2.14.0 and 2.14.1, and full trace export for affected trace ids. Assign owner: @liang-platform for runtime rollback verification, @marta-sre for SLO dashboard update and customer comms.

marta-sre: tagging eng-runtime for RC: @liang-platform please ping if you need dedicated infra.

liang-platform: ack. I'll follow up with a short runbook entry: quick rollback (canary->0%), bump sampling, verify p99 returns to baseline, then schedule a proper revert/patch.

raj-support: customer updated: appreciated the quick response, will wait for RCA.

observability-bot: NOTE: SLO p99 back to 2.8s after canary throttled (5m check). Closing alert if stable for 30m.

marta-sre: creating follow-up ticket for detailed postmortem and action items. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
